item.title: Justin Jefferson will play for Vikings, Jordan Addison and Odell Beckham Jr. will not
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: All of Sunday's 1 p.m. ET inactives have been announced.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings had both of their top wide receivers listed as questionable on their final injury report of Week 5 and the gameday decisions went in different directions.

Justin Jefferson will play after missing last Sunday's win over the Dolphins with an ankle injury, but Jordan Addison will miss the game with a hamstring injury. There was some thought that Odell Beckham Jr. would make his Vikings debut on Sunday, but he is also inactive.

Beckham signed to the practice squad this week and was elevated on Saturday, but Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said he'd only play if the team was missing one of the other wideouts. They are, but Beckham is still out of the lineup. Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price, and practice squad elevation Jeshaun Jones are the other wideouts.

item.title: After playing in London, Colts have an added disadvantage on Sunday at Steelers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL schedule is a 272-piece jigsaw puzzle with millions of potential configurations and no one arrangement of pieces that will be completely fair and equitable to all 32 teams.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL schedule is a 272-piece jigsaw puzzle with millions of potential configurations and no one arrangement of pieces that will be completely fair and equitable to all 32 teams.

The Week 4 and Week 5 games in 2026 include a glitch about which the Colts should not be thrilled.

They got the shoulder tap to fly to London for a game against the Commanders last Sunday. This week, after returning from England, the Colts travel to Pittsburgh for a game against the Steelers.

Meanwhile, the Steelers had a bus trip to and from Cleveland for a Week 4 Thursday night game, followed by a mini-bye while their next foe was playing overseas.

It's a basic issue of competitive integrity that will take a back seat to the ongoing obsession with global expansion. And the league will gloss over such irregularities because there's nothing that can be done to eliminate the annoyances and inconveniences that come from expecting teams to make long trips for games on foreign soil and to return home for the next game on the slate.

That's one of the reasons why the league hopes to get clearance from the NFL Players Association to stage 16 international games per year. If every team has to travel to and from another country once per season, the hassle is largely balanced out.

Still, there's something to be said for also ensuring that any team that plays on a given Sunday in another country will be facing on the following Sunday a team that played on Sunday or Monday, and not on the preceding Thursday. That part was avoidable for the 2026 schedule — and it was not avoided.

item.title: Darius Cooper 62-yard touchdown gives Eagles lead over Jaguars in London
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Eagles took their first lead of the game on another big play from Cooper.
item.content:encoded:
All Darius Cooper does is catch touchdowns.

Cooper scored another one today in London, a 62-yarder from Jalen Hurts that gave the Eagles a 14-7 lead over the Jaguars.

Cooper now has six catches this season, and four of them are touchdowns. He scored two touchdowns last week against the Rams and one in Week 2 against the Titans.

Cooper made the Eagles' roster last season as an undrafted rookie out of Tarleton State, and he's showing he belongs in the NFL.

Now the Jaguars have to show something in London, where the Eagles have come to life.

item.title: Eagles omitted Lane Johnson from public list of inactive players for Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Eagles' decision to keep retired right tackle Lane Johnson on the 53-man roster for the rest of the season could create more than a little confusion.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles' decision to keep retired right tackle Lane Johnson on the 53-man roster for the rest of the season could create more than a little confusion. On Sunday morning, it already created some.

When the team posted its “full list” of inactive players for the Week 5 game against the Jaguars, Johnson's name wasn't mentioned. Which implied to the world that Johnson was officially active for the game, despite his announced retirement.

Per the Eagles, Johnson is one of inactive players. Per the league, Johnson was specifically listed as inactive for the game in the team's communications with the league.

So why not put him on the list of inactive players?

It's something to watch with each upcoming game. If the Eagles are going to keep Johnson on the roster despite his retirement, they probably shouldn't treat him as retired but as a player who remains on the team in their public releases.

item.title: Will Shipley touchdown run ties Eagles and Jaguars 7-7 in London
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Shipley's score was the first first-half touchdown the Jaguars' defense has allowed this season.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles have evened the score this morning in London.

Eagles running back Will Shipley ran in a two-yard touchdown to tie the Jaguars 7-7.

The Eagles had previously thrown an incompletion on third down that would have resulted in them settling for a field goal, but Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter was flagged for pass interference, giving the Eagles first-and-goal.

Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik suffered a shoulder injury on his first snap of the game and was replaced by defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton. Hamilton's first snap, an extra point, was high, but punter Logan Cooke grabbed it and placed it well enough for Cam Little to make the kick. Hamilton's second snap, a punt, was perfect.

item.title: Vikings' touchdown drought isn't keeping them from winning
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 4-0 Vikings have turned the page back to the days of the Purple People Eaters.
item.content:encoded:
The 4-0 Vikings have turned the page back to the days of the Purple People Eaters. And the stout defense isn't getting a ton of help from the offense.

The Vikings have had 18 straight drives without a touchdown. The last one happened in the second quarter of a Week 3 win over the Buccaneers. The Week 4 victory over the Dolphins happened with five field goals.

Yes, tight end T.J. Hockenson could have scored just before the two-minute warning, but he wisely took a knee and allowed the Vikings to ensure the Dolphins wouldn't be able to score twice and steal the game. Either way, the Vikings did not register a touchdown against the Dolphins.

As noted last Sunday, the win made the Vikings the first team in more than 100 years to start 4-0 despite not scoring a touchdown in multiple games. The 1922 and 1923 Chicago Cardinals were the only other teams to accomplish that feat.

If the Vikings do it again at any point this year, they'll become only the fourth team in NFL history to win three or more games without scoring a touchdown. The others were the 1922 Chicago Cardinals, the 1923 Chicago Bears, and the 1993 Indianapolis Colts, per NBC Sports research.

The all-time record, held by the 1922 Cardinals, is four.

Still, there's reason to believe the Vikings could snap out of their early-season funk. After the Dolphins scored a touchdown late in the third quarter to cut Minnesota's lead to 12-10, the Vikings offense seemed to wake up. A 15-play, 60-yard drive consumed more than eight minutes of clock time and extended the lead to 15-10. Then, after a three-and-out effort from the Dolphins, the Vikings burned the remaining 5:41 by moving the ball 79 yards from their own 19 to the Miami two.

The next test comes today, in New Orleans. The 1-3 Saints are desperate for a win after losing their first two home games of the season — capped by Monday night's embarrassing loss to the Falcons. New Orleans hasn't lost its first three games at home since 1995.

item.title: Jaguars take 7-0 lead on 51-yard touchdown catch-and-run by Parker Washington
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Washington's big play put the Jaguars on the board first in London.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington had the first big play in London today. At least, the first big play that wasn't called back by a penalty.

Washington caught a short pass from Trevor Lawrence and raced through the Eagles' secondary for a 51-yard touchdown to give Jacksonville a 7-0 lead.

On the play just before that one, Jaguars wide receiver Travis Hunter caught a nine-yard pass on second-and-7, a rare offensive contribution for the two-way player who has played mostly defense this season.

The Jaguars' drive started when the Eagles were stopped on fourth-and-1, on a surprising play call when they had Jalen Hurts in the shotgun and handing off to running back Will Shipley, rather than taking it himself on the tush push.

Now the Eagles' much-maligned offense needs to get something going.

item.title: Eagles' Jeremiah Trotter, Jaguars' Bryan Thomas ejected on opening kickoff
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A crazy start in London saw a kickoff return touchdown called back on a holding penalty.
item.content:encoded:
Today's game in London had the craziest beginning of any NFL game this season.

The opening kickoff was returned for a touchdown by Jacksonville's Josh Cameron, but it was called back by a holding penalty. But that wasn't even the crazy part.

During the chaos as the officials started to call everyone back to re-do the kickoff, Philadelphia's Jeremiah Trotter and Jacksonville's Bryan Thomas fought in the middle of the field, and both were ejected, before an official play had even been run.

It's a loud and mostly pro-Eagles crowd in London, and fans who got to their seats late missed something wild.

item.title: Report: Some doctors believe Jayden Daniels risks another elbow dislocation
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels returns on Sunday, three weeks after suffering a second dislocation of his left elbow in the past 11 months.
item.content:encoded:
Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels returns on Sunday, three weeks after suffering a second dislocation of his left elbow in the past 11 months.

The move comes with a calculated risk. Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, "[t]here are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if" Daniels suffers a third dislocation of the elbow.

Although none of the doctors who expressed that concern have actually examined Daniels (which, in most cases, means that they should politely shut the hell up), it's fairly obvious that the thing that has happened to Daniels twice could happen again. In both instances, he extended his left arm while falling. On impact with the ground, the elbow went out of joint. So, yes, there's something in the elbow that makes it susceptible to dislocation when he uses the arm to brace himself.

Daniels will wear a brace on his non-throwing elbow. Whether it matters won't be known until the next time he falls and tries to brace himself with his left arm.

The problem for Daniels, and the Commanders, is that surgery likely would be the only way to fix the problem. With Daniels eligible for a second contract after the 2026 season, he needs to play as many games as possible (and play well) to unlock a significant deal.

The coaching staff also has plenty of reasons to let him risk it, especially with Marcus Mariota injured. Dan Quinn has been around long enough to know that, if 2026 goes the way 2025 did, he won't be around in 2027.

The Eagles ruled out a slew of players ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London, so there wasn't much mystery to their inactive list ahead of kickoff.

The one question mark was linebacker Jonathan Greenard, although the fact that he didn't practice all week due to an ankle injury pointed in a clear direction. Greenard is inactive for the game along with wide receiver Hollywood Brown, wide receiver DeVonta Smith, running back Saquon Barkley, safety Marcus Epps and center Drew Kendall.

While Lane Johnson announced his retirement this week and will not play, he remains on the Eagles' roster and was not included on the list of inactives the team released 90 minutes ahead of kickoff. Rookie quarterback Cole Payton is also active for the first time this season.

Wide receiver C.J. Williams, cornerback Alijah Huzzie, safety Eric Murray, cornerback Jaylon Jones, offensive lineman Daniel Faalele, defensive end Wesley Williams, and defensive tackle Albert Regis are inactive for Jacksonville.

item.title: Eagles will keep Lane Johnson on the roster until June 2, for cap purposes
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: What's the best way for the Eagles to avoid a salary-cap mess in 2027 due to the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson?
item.content:encoded:
What's the best way for the Eagles to avoid a salary-cap mess in 2027 due to the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson? Behave as if he didn't retire, of course.

We floated that idea both on PFT Live and in this item after Johnson unexpectedly retired from football this week. Placement of Johnson on the reserve/retired list would result in the Eagles taking the full acceleration of all past payments (signing bonus and option bonus). Keeping him on the roster avoids that outcome until 2028.

And so, via Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL, the Eagles will keep Johnson on the roster until June 2.

It's a little surprising that they're not coming up with a way to shift him to the non-football injury/illness list. That would invite inevitable gripes from other teams, who would accuse the Eagles of doing exactly what they're doing — avoiding the 2027 cap mess while also clearing out the roster spot. And so they'll willingly reduce their roster limit to 52 for the balance of the season in order to preserve the ability to delay the bulk of the cap hit until 2028.

The most immediate impact of that decision happened in the quarterback room. They trimmed the depth chart from three to two by cutting veteran backup Andy Dalton, who was No. 2 until he threw an interception in the red zone while starter Jalen Hurts was getting a concussion evaluation in the Week 3 Monday night loss at Chicago.

Keeping Johnson on the roster means that they won't be able to declare that Johnson has committed a forfeitable breach and recover some of his signing-bonus money. Rapoport notes that, as to the $21.7 million option bonus Johnson earned earlier this year, Johnson will "pay back several million dollars -- with the exact number to be determined."

As we explained earlier this week, the option bonus was split into two payments: $10.85 million paid within 15 days of the exercise of the option bonus and $10.85 million paid on or before December 1, 2026. Johnson will likely give up some, or perhaps even all, of the unpaid amount. Given that the $21.7 million had been part of his 2026 salary with the option bonus used as a way to layer the cap consequences, it was advance pay for a full season of service. By choosing to retire with 14 weeks left in the season, it's more than reasonable for Johnson to give up half of the advance payment.

Could the Eagles have played hardball with Johnson, putting him on the reserve/retired list and seeking repayment of millions in signing bonus and option bonus? Yes. Beyond the fact that bullying one of the franchise's all-time greats into giving back so much money (then again, that didn't stop the Lions when Barry Sanders retired — or when Calvin Johnson retired), it would have sparked a full acceleration of all remaining payments previously made (minus whatever they recover) in 2027.

That's the biggest flaw in the much-ballyhooed "financial hack" of using a stream of option bonuses in big-money veteran contracts to manage the cap. An unexpected retirement can handcuff the front office, to the point at which (as it's doing with Johnson) the team behaves as if the retirement didn't happen until the right moment arrives to officially process the move.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets will remain shorthanded on offense for Sunday's game against the Browns.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets will remain shorthanded on offense for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Friday that running back Breece Hall and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell have been ruled out. It's the second game in a row that Hall will miss with a quad injury and Mitchell has been out with a finger injury since Week 2.

The Jets are set to get tight end Mason Taylor back. He missed the last two games with a thumb injury, but has practiced all this week and is on track to play. Wide receiver Tim Patrick could also make his 2026 debut after being designated for return from injured reserve this week.

Guard Dylan Parham (knee) and linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad) will also miss the game for the Jets.

item.title: Jeremiah Smith is the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Ohio State wide receiver has moved ahead of Arch Manning and is now favored to go first overall.
item.content:encoded:
No wide receiver has been the first overall pick in the NFL draft since Keyshawn Johnson in 1996. Jeremiah Smith may do it in 2027.

Smith, the Ohio State wide receiver, is now the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, with +300 odds. On Saturday, Smith put up another good performance, catching four passes for 93 yards and two touchdowns in a win over Maryland.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning, who had been the betting favorite to go first overall, had a rough game in Saturday's loss to Oklahoma. Manning is now second in the betting odds to go first overall in 2027, at +350.

Next in the odds is Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr at +380. Carr completed 14 of 20 passes for 181 yards, with three touchdowns and no interceptions, plus 41 rushing yards, in Saturday's 58-7 win over Stanford.

Following Carr in the betting odds are Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss at +600, Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker at +650, Miami quarterback Darian Mensah at +750 and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore at +1200.

item.title: Kirk Cousins is having a rare debut run with the Raiders
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Now with his fourth NFL team, quarterback Kirk Cousins has made a significant initial impact in Las Vegas.
item.content:encoded:
Now with his fourth NFL team, quarterback Kirk Cousins has made a significant initial impact in Las Vegas.

His 11 touchdown passes in four games ties Cousins with 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy for the NFL lead. If Cousins gets three more on Sunday for the Raiders against the Patriots, he would join a club that currently consists of only two quarterbacks.

Via NBC Sports research, Patrick Mahomes, with the Chiefs, and Kurt Warner, with the Rams, are the only quarterbacks to throw 14 or more touchdown passes in their first five games with a given franchise. Both won the MVP award in the year they accomplished that feat.

If Cousins can keep it going, he'll eventually force his way into the MVP conversation. Which could result in a 38-year-old quarterback winning his first MVP award, one year after a 37-year-old quarterback (Matthew Stafford) won his first MVP award.

There's still a long way to go. Winning in New England on Sunday, a week after the Raiders' first loss of the season, would definitely help Cousins's cause.

item.title: Matt LaFleur takes 12-3 record vs. Bears into Sunday's showdown
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Bears coach Ben Johnson has made it clear that he doesn't like the Packers.
item.content:encoded:
Bears coach Ben Johnson has made it clear that he doesn't like the Packers. Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur has given the Bears plenty of reasons not to like the Packers.

Since arriving as head coach of the Packers in 2019, LaFleur has a 12-3 record against the Bears, including the postseason. His 80 percent win rate is the highest that any coach has ever generated against the Bears, with a minimum of 10 games played.

Johnson, of course, has won the last two — late in the 2025 regular season and then in the wild-card round. The Bears haven't beaten the Packers three times in a row since 2005-06. They're favored to win at Lambeau Field for the first time in 20 years.

Chicago's defense has become a real strength. The Bears have gone three straight games allowing 12 or fewer points. The last team to do that for four games in a row was the 2017 Eagles, who'd go on to win the Super Bowl that year.

item.title: Trevor Lawrence continues to perform among the NFL's elite quarterbacks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The hiring of Liam Coen as head coach of the Jaguars has been very good for quarterback Trevor Lawrence.
item.content:encoded:
The hiring of Liam Coen as head coach of the Jaguars has been very good for quarterback Trevor Lawrence. After Coen arrived, Lawrence became one of the elite quarterbacks in the NFL.

Case in point: Lawrence has produced more touchdowns since the start of the 2025 season than all NFL quarterbacks except two: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford and Bills quarterback Josh Allen.

Via NBC Sports research, Lawrence has 49 total touchdowns (40 passing, nine rushing). Stafford and Allen have 58 each.

The Jaguars have also won 11 of their last 13 games. That gives them the best record in the AFC over that span. And, on Sunday morning, they'll play their 15th game in London — three times more than any other NFL team.

Their record in London is 7-7. And they'll play their next two there, against the Eagles in Week 5 and the Texans in Week 6.

item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's not clear where receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will be playing as of next week.
item.content:encoded:
It's not clear where receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will be playing as of next week. It's becoming more and more clear he won't be playing for the Cardinals.

Via Josh Weinfuss of ESPN, Harrison was not present for team meetings on Saturday night.

Harrison reportedly has been told he won't be active for Sunday's game against the Lions, as a trade is finalized.

Some in league circles believe he'll be traded to the Texans. Some think the Raiders could be lurking. Sunday's games could shake things up, based on injuries that could happen in the various games.

Regardless, it's hard to imagine Harrison staying with the Cardinals given these developments. At this point, it's just a matter of the Cardinals getting the best return they can for the fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft.

item.title: Rams aren't likely to return Myles Garrett to practice this week
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The update that Rams coach Sean McVay promised on Monday to deliver on Thursday regarding defensive end Myles Garrett arrived on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
The update that Rams coach Sean McVay promised on Monday to deliver on Thursday regarding defensive end Myles Garrett arrived on Saturday.

Garrett, who landed on injured reserve after Week 1 due to knee surgery, can return to practice after Week 5, the fourth game he'll miss. The Rams currently don't plan to open his practice window.

“He’s making good progress, but what I will say is he's not ready to say whether we'll open that window or not," McVay told reporters on Saturday. "[T]he surgery went really well. He's making good progress as far as what that timeline looks like. It's week to week in terms of how he feels, but I would say it's more likely that we do not start his clock next week. When I talk to Neal ElAttrache, and I think it's a great way to articulate it, there's a difference between return to play and return to performance. When you do something like this, let's put him in a good position to return to performance. Part of that will be once he gets to those benchmarks where he's hitting all the benchmarks that we want, then let's physically put him in a position to do things that are in alignment with playing football, see how the knee responds, which we expect it to respond well and then that's when you can really start talking about, ‘Okay, he's going to play for us,’ and things of that nature.”

McVay also was asked whether the lack of practice time in training camp will be a factor in the decision.

“I think a lot of that was because we were trying to manage a situation that we're hoping to be able to work through," McVay said. "A lot of that really stemmed from the irritation in the knee so hopefully that's gone and it’s really, how quickly can the alien get up to speed for us? But, no, I think because we got that fixed and because he's feeling so good, I think that'll be an accelerated process. Him actually doing football-related activities and drills will be very important for us to put him in a position to join the group and be the guy that we're accustomed to seeing and that he wants to be for this team as well.”

Garrett apparently ignored the knee issue until he got into the game against the 49ers in Australia and realized it wasn't something he could play through. That resulted in the fairly quick decision to have the knee surgically repaired, with the goal of getting the 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year up to speed and ready to do what the Rams hope he'll be able to do.

With Garrett unlikely to return to practice this week, that means he'll miss the Week 6 game against the Cardinals. After that, the Rams play the Raders, Chargers, Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals again before their Week 11 bye.

item.title: Packers will honor Mike Ditka with a moment of silence before Sunday's game vs. Bears
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Packers will host the Bears on Sunday, two days after the passing of legendary coach Mike Ditka.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers will host the Bears on Sunday, two days after the passing of legendary coach Mike Ditka. And the Packers will be paying their respects to their former nemesis.

Via Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times, the Packers will honor Ditka with a moment of silence.

“One of the fiercest competitors in NFL history, Mike helped define the intensity and tradition of the Packers-Bears rivalry, the oldest in professional football,” the Packers said in a statement. “He embodied the toughness and passion that have made the rivalry one of the most storied in all of sports.

“While he was a formidable opponent, his contributions to the game and to a rivalry that has meant so much to both franchises will always be respected and remembered by the Green Bay Packers.”

Ditka had a 15-5 record against the Packers during his eleven years as head coach of the Bears. The two games in his first season of 1982 were lost to a players' strike.

The Bears under Ditka swept the Packers in 1985, 1986, 1987, 1988, 1990, and 1991.

item.title: NFL fines Quinn Meinerz for posting notice of drug test after flattening Aaron Donald
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: During the Week 3 win over the Rams, Broncos offensive lineman Quinn Meinerz manhandled L.A. defensive tackle Aaron Donald.
item.content:encoded:
During the Week 3 win over the Rams, Broncos offensive lineman Quinn Meinerz manhandled L.A. defensive tackle Aaron Donald. Meinerz promptly received a notice of a drug test — and he posted it on social media.

To no surprise, the NFL has responded by disciplining Meinerz.

Via Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post, Meinerz was fined $15,000 for posting the notice of the PED test. Gabriel adds that Meinerz is appealing the punishment.

The current policy is as clear as it can be: "[A]ny recording or photography of any stage of the collection process via any media (audio or visual), including but not limited to screen shots of testing notifications, video of the collectors or the collection of a specimen, and sharing such information via any social media is not permitted. A player found in violation of the rule prohibiting unauthorized recording of the collection process and sharing such information on social media will be subject to a fine of $15,000."

That's what Meinerz did. The negotiated terms of the PED policy prohibit it. The situation is as open and shut as it can be.

item.title: Sunday's games could become a significant factor in the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: One injury could alter everything, as to Harrison's eventual destination.
item.content:encoded:
The #insiders told us on Saturday morning that Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will soon be traded. They didn't however, share the destination.

With Harrison reportedly due to be inactive on Sunday versus the Lions as the trade details are finalized, Sunday's full slate of games could potentially reshuffle the deck.

Many believe the Texans are the team that will be trading for Harrison, a move that would reunite him with former Ohio State teammate C.J. Stroud. But what if the Texans lose to the Titans? Could Houston decide at that point to not devote future assets to a season that could be a lost cause?

Likewise, if Stroud is injured on Sunday, the whole "Buckeye reunion" vibe would be significantly diminished.

Then there's the possibility that a contender will lose a starting receiver due to injury during Sunday's games. Suddenly, a team that wasn't in the mix for Harrison could revisit its position, quickly.

Nothing is ever done until it's done. Sunday's games could change the entire dynamic for a Harrison trade.

For now, the league-wide speculation points to the Texans as the destination for Harrison. Some, however, think the Raiders could be lurking. Either way, Sunday's action could become a factor in the eventual transaction, with the only surprise at this point being Harrison not being traded.

item.title: John Franklin-Myers was fined only $12,537 for kneeing Derrick Henry in the stomach
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The weekly list of NFL-imposed fines for Week 4 includes Titans defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers.
item.content:encoded:
The weekly list of NFL-imposed fines for Week 4 includes Titans defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers. On the surface, the $12,537 fine for "striking/kicking/kneeing" seems as perfunctory as any such fine ever does.

The video paints a different picture.

It happened in the second quarter of Sunday's game between the Titans and the Ravens, on a play that resulted in a three-yard touchdown pass from Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson to tight end Mark Andrews. Although the game broadcast didn't capture it, the film reveals the full incident. Ravens running back Derrick Henry cut-blocked Franklin-Myers. After the ball was caught in the end zone, and while Henry was on all fours and not looking, Franklin-Myers took a step back and then jammed his knee into Henry's midsection.

The officials presumably didn't see it, because no penalty flag was thrown. It was the kind of gratuitous move that could have resulted in an ejection. It's somewhat surprising it didn't lead to a suspension.

The end result doesn't come close to matching the infraction. It's less than the league fined Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Browns running back Quinshon Judkins for a celebration that mimed smoking a joint. And it was nearly half the amount of a fine that was imposed earlier this season, we're told, on Ravens receiver LaJohntay Wester for — God forbid — displaying an unauthorized logo on his gloves.

Those fines aren't part of the weekly announcement from the league. Wester was fined $23,882 after the Ravens' Week 1 game against the Colts for the foreign logo on his gloves.

While the fine schedule is negotiated between the NFL and the NFL Players Association, something is off if a player can deliberately ram a knee into the midsection of an unsuspecting opponent and be fined only $12,537, but having an unauthorized logo on the official gloves costs $23,882.

item.title: Legendary player, coach Mike Ditka dies at 86
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Ditka was a larger-than-life figure, in Chicago and beyond.
item.content:encoded:
Hall of Famer Mike Ditka, the legendary coach of the 1985 Bears, has died. He was 86.

Via ESPN, Ditka's family announced his passing on Friday morning.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," Ditka's family said. "While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.

"Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."

An Aliquippa, Pennsylvania, native who played college football at Pitt, Ditka was the first tight end to be inducted into the Hall of Fame. As a rookie in 1961, he was the first tight end in NFL history to generate 1,000 receiving yards in a season.

As a player, Ditka was a member of the Bears' 1963 NFL Championship team. He also played for the 1971 Cowboys, who won Super Bowl VI.

After a 12-year playing career, Ditka joined the Cowboys as an assistant coach. In 1982, he became the head coach of the Bears.

Ditka became a larger-than-life figure in Chicago, and beyond. He oozed football, and his temperament matched the intensity of the game.

The Bears fired Ditka after the 1992 season. He became head coach of the Saints in 1997. He negotiated the famous Ricky Williams trade, in which the Saints gave up all of their 1999 draft (and another first-rounder) to get the Heisman Trophy winner from Texas.

Ditka also worked for NBC and ESPN, as an analyst.

We extend our condolences to Ditka's family, friends, players, colleagues, and to the Bears and their fans.

item.title: Bears: Mike Ditka is an "icon" whose impact will last "for generations"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The man who led the 1985 Bears to a Super Bowl win died on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
The man who led the 1985 Bears to a Super Bowl win died on Friday. The team with which he is most associated issued a statement following Ditka's passing.

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of legendary and treasured Chicago Bear and Pro Football Hall of Famer Mike Ditka," the Bears said. "Mike's impact on the Chicago Bears organization, over decades as a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organization, is immeasurable. His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations.

"We extend our love, prayers, and heartfelt condolences to the Ditka family, and join all Bears fans in deep sadness and reverence as we remember and honor Mike Ditka."

That accurately summarizes Ditka's impact on the Bears and Chicago. He presided over a magical time for the Bears, and the NFL.

He was brash. He was boisterous. He was effective. And he led the Bears to their only Super Bowl title in franchise history.

item.title: Tyreek Hill's current civil trial complicates his effort to return to NFL
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Thursday, Hill admitted to shoving his ex-wife into a wall.
item.content:encoded:
The week began with a flurry of news regarding receiver Tyreek Hill's supposedly imminent return to the NFL. Then, reality set in.

The NFL's pending Personal Conduct Policy investigation of Hill based on abuse allegations made by his ex-wife, Keeta Vaccaro, has taken a back seat to a civil trial that started on Tuesday. In it, Vaccaro seeks compensation for multiple instances of assault and battery.

On Thursday, Hill testified. Via Xuan Thai of ESPN, Hill admitted to pushing Vaccaro against a wall.

"I told her that night, I said, 'Don't you ever touch me in your life,'" Hill said on the witness stand. "I pushed her against the wall, and I tried to force her to get off me. I created a hole in the wall trying to force her to get off me that night."

Hill clearly sees pushing Vaccaro into a wall hard enough to put a hole in it as a reasonable act of self-defense. The NFL may not agree with his assessment.

He also admitted threatening Vaccaro. Hill said he was "deeply ashamed" for saying that he was "able to get people to hurt her." (He had no choice but to admit to saying it; his words were recorded and preserved.)

Hill denied Vaccaro's allegation that he hit her, scratched her, shoved her (other than the admission that he pushed her into a wall hard enough to create a hole), spit in her face, or tried to punch her in the stomach while she was pregnant. While that may persuade a jury to exonerate him, the NFL will make its own assessment as to whether he did or didn't do the things Vaccaro has accused him of doing.

If, in the end, the NFL's investigators believe Vaccaro more than they believe Hill, he could be facing a significant suspension. In theory, each incident of alleged abuse could spark a six-game baseline suspension.

Then there's Hill's history, dating back to the 2015 guilty plea to domestic assault and battery by strangulation in an incident involving his then-pregnant girlfriend and a still-unresolved 2019 incident that left his young son with a broken arm. While the jury in the ongoing case may not hear evidence as to those situations, the NFL knows all about them. And they will likely influence the league's assessment of Hill's credibility — and they could result in enhanced discipline.

The trial testimony to date makes the out-of-the-blue effort to get Hill on an NFL team even more strange. Whatever the strategy for introducing the notion of Hill signing with the Chiefs or some other team on the eve of the civil trial, the civil trial significantly complicates his desire to play again.

Even if the NFL doesn't choose to banish him with the opportunity to apply for reinstatement after a year — the strongest punishment available under the Personal Conduct Policy — what team in its right mind would sign him after the testimony of the past few days?

item.title: As Bears intend to build a dome, Mike Ditka would not approve
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The passing of larger-than-life NFL legend Mike Ditka has sparked a flood of great stories and clips from Ditka's time in football.
item.content:encoded:
The passing of larger-than-life NFL legend Mike Ditka has sparked a flood of great stories and clips from Ditka's time in football. Many of them stand out. There's one that's particularly relevant to the Bears' ongoing quest to vacate Soldier Field for a venue with a roof.

In December 1987, as the Bears prepared for their annual trip to the Metrodome in Minneapolis, Ditka went off on football not played in the elements.

"I just don’t like indoor domes," Ditka said. "They weren't meant for football. Football is meant to play it outside and on grass. . . . Indoor domes should be useful for roller rinks. That's all they should be for. Roller skating."

That same week, Ditka skated through the Bears' offices in rollerblades.

"They were a gift," Ditka said. "[Vikings G.M.] Mike Lynn sprung for them. That might refute everything I've heard about him from his players."

The Bears won the "Rollerdome" game, 30-24, on a late touchdown pass from Mike Tomczak to Dennis Gentry.

"I did what I did about the dome for certain reasons," Ditka said after the victory. "To get the pressure off the players and get it on me. And I think for that point, it worked."

Ditka then made a point that hopefully will resonate with today's coaches.

"If people don't like the things I do, that's just a point of life," Ditka said. "There's gotta be some levity in life, and there's gotta be a little bit of fun had. And we take this whole thing seriously, like it's life and death. It's not life and death. We're gonna go out and play as hard as we can. We're gonna be great representatives of the city of Chicago, the Chicago Bear organization. That's all we're trying to do is be something that people can be proud of. But, you know, if I'm not gonna have any fun on my way there, partner, I just — they got the wrong guy, because, you know, I said a long time ago, maybe the NFL is a little bit too staid and true in its ways. Maybe it takes somebody to loosen them up a little bit. And our players do that, so why shouldn't the coach be a little wacky?"

Current Bears coach Ben Johnson seems to already be living that message. With the first game after Ditka's passing coming against the Packers at Lambeau Field, maybe Johnson will take it up a notch.

Back to Ditka's point. Football really is meant to be played outside and on grass. Unfortunately, the indoor ship seems to have sailed. The Commanders, Browns, Titans, and Chiefs are currently moving toward swapping the elements for a roller rink. And the Bears inevitably will join them, whether that's in Chicago, Arlington Heights, or Hammond, Indiana.

Whoever the coach of the Vikings is at the time should show up for the first game to be played there on roller skates, as the ultimate homage to Ditka.

item.title: Report: Cardinals will be trading receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The team hasn't been named; the thinking is it's the Texans.
item.content:encoded:
Another 2024 top-10 draft pick is about to be on the move.

According to ESPNFL, the Cardinals will be trading receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Harrison, per the report, will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions, as the details are finalized.

The current chatter in league circles is that Harrison will land in Houston, where he'd be reunited with former Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud.

The Cardinals, we're told, had been looking for a package that includes a second-round pick. Whether they get that remains to be seen.

And it's definitely unusual for the news of a trade to emerge without a destination. It could be an eleventh-hour attempt to get other teams to the table, in the hopes of driving up the price.

When the trade happens, Harrison will join former Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who was taken tenth overall in 2024, as players traded fairly quickly by the teams that took them.

Harrison has become largely forgotten in the Arizona offense under new coach Mike LaFleur. In four games this season, he has five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown.

item.title: Texans are the likely destination for Marvin Harrison Jr.
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Negotiations have focused on second-round pick in 2028 vs. second-round pick in 2027.
item.content:encoded:
The Cardinal are working on a trade for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., with the destination currently unknown.

The speculation for now centers on the Texans, per multiple sources.

For whatever reason, the Cardinals are keeping that under wraps. They could be hoping to get someone else to make a better offer, or they could be hoping to squeeze a little more out of the Texans before a deal is done.

The trade, if it happens, will reunited Harrison with Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud. They spent multiple years together at Ohio State.

The package is expected to include a second-round pick. The Texans, we're told, had offered a second-round pick in 2028. The Cardinals have been pushing for a second-round pick in 2027.

It seems inevitable at this point that Harrison will be traded; the cat has well escaped the bag. And it should surprise no one if/when it's the Texans — unless some other team out there makes a late play with a better package of picks.

item.title: Arch Manning's two fourth-quarter interceptions doom Texas in loss to Oklahoma
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Texas is No. 1 no more, after a two-interception fourth quarter from quarterback Arch Manning handed Oklahoma a come-from-behind victory in the Red River Rivalry.
item.content:encoded:
Texas is No. 1 no more, after a two-interception fourth quarter from quarterback Arch Manning handed Oklahoma a come-from-behind victory in the Red River Rivalry.

The Longhorns led 17-7 at halftime, but the second half was a disaster for Manning and Texas, and Oklahoma won 27-24 with a field goal as time expired. Texas entered the game 4-0 and the top-ranked team in the country; Oklahoma entered 2-2 and unranked.

Texas punted on all three of its third-quarter possessions, and in the fourth quarter, Manning threw two interceptions. The first was a pick-six that gave Oklahoma its first lead of the game, and the second set up Oklahoma's game-winning field goal.

Manning's numbers -- 19 of 31 for 260 yards, with three touchdowns and two interceptions, plus 20 rushing yards -- don't look terrible. But his fourth quarter performance is what will be remembered from this game.

Manning is the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the NFL draft, just like his uncles Peyton and Eli were. He didn't look like a first overall pick today.

item.title: NFL issues season-high 10 fines for player safety fouls in Week 4
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The NFL's announced Week 4 fines featured a season-high 10 infractions for player safety fouls that qualify toward a possible suspension.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's announced Week 4 fines featured a season-high 10 infractions for player safety fouls that qualify toward a possible suspension.

Ravens linebacker Trenton Simpson was fined $17,911 for a horsecollar tackle.

Browns defensive tackle Adin Huntington ($5,620), Lions linebacker Jack Campbell ($15,930), Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick ($17,911), Jets defensive end Darrell Jackson ($6,683) and Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori ($14,648) were fined for hip-drop tackles.

Cowboys cornerback Reddy Steward ($5,583), Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter ($13,639) and Rams linebacker Nate Landman ($11,111) were fined for a hit on a defenseless player.

Broncos offensive lineman Ben Powers was docked $17,911 for a blindside block.

Three fines in any one category trigger an automatic one-game suspension. Players can appeal the fines.
